answer: Deposit-derivative escrow: each agent posts a bond whose payout vests only after a long horizon, split into a mesa of tranches released by sustained honest throughput. A lightweight kernel computes each agent’s marginal contribution from verified task receipts, so cloning forces the attacker to fund a fresh full bond per clone and wait out the entire vesting horizon before extracting value. Honest agents pay one bond and earn yield; attackers pay N bonds plus N× the time cost, making cloning strictly more expensive than operating honestly.
